text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for tenant 'NimblePay' — reserved_capacity_throttle on ded-nyc-3. Symptoms: queue latency 95p > 1.2s, 5xx spike, burst of small requests. Alert rule: reserved-pool-queue-saturation.
pd-bot: Incident INC-2145 created and paged oncall@eng.urgency=high, escalation policy=dedicated-tenant-escalation.
maya: ack'd. I'm oncall for the next 30m. pulling metrics + logs now.
jon: standing by for creds/route changes.
sandeep: seeing KV cache evictions jump ~x8 over baseline and queue depth climb on ded-nyc-3. suspect short-tail request storm from NimblePay's webhook batcher.
maya: confirmed elevated eviction_count and backpressure counters. sample logs:
```
2026-03-14T10:09:48Z ded-nyc-3 svc: enqueue timeout tenant=NimblePay id=0x8a3f err=queue_full
2026-03-14T10:10:02Z ded-nyc-3 runtime: kvcache.evictions=812 -> 6800 within 3m
2026-03-14T10:10:14Z ded-nyc-3 proxy: 502 upstream write error tenant=NimblePay route=/v1/payments
```
ops-runbook-bot: Suggested mitigations (ordered): 1) add temporary route fallback to general pool, 2) enable tenant burst reserve if available, 3) apply client-side rate limit via edge rule, 4) increase KV cache retention window. Runbook link: https://console.internal/runbooks/dedicated-throttle.
tara: what's customer-visible impact? are payments failing?
maya: initial customer report from support: ~12% reqs hitting 5xx on /v1/payments (payment submission). Errors started 10:02 UTC, spike peaked 10:11. Affects ~NimblePay production cluster only.
sandeep: can try immediate temporary burst increase — API: `redwoodctl reserved set-burst --tenant NimblePay --pool ded-nyc-3 --tokens 30` (needs ops token). downside: higher cost and may push pressure to other tenants on same host if oversubscribed.
jon: I have ops token. running command now.
jon: `> redwoodctl reserved set-burst --tenant NimblePay --pool ded-nyc-3 --tokens 30 --reason \"auto-pager response\"`
jon: response: `OK: burst tokens allocated until 2026-03-14T11:00:00Z`
maya: enabling route fallback to general inference pool for non-critical endpoints to reduce ded-nyc-3 load. applying rule: `edgectl route update --tenant NimblePay --match \"/v1/health*\" --to general-pool` (testing first).
maya: rolling out fallback in canary.
incident-bot: Automated fallback policy triggered: 4/5 canary hosts updated, no errors. routing shift ~18% of traffic off ded-nyc-3.
sandeep: post-burst and routing change metrics: queue depth down 60%, 5xx rate down from 12% -> 2.1% in last 3m. KV evictions trending down.
tara: do we need to engage account/PE to notify NimblePay? expected user impact reduced but payments still affected at low rate.
maya: yes, send a short note to account and support. I'll draft: \"We experienced a transient reserved-pool saturation impacting some payment requests; we've applied temporary burst capacity and rerouted non-critical traffic. We're monitoring; next update in 15m.\"
jon: taking over hands-on at 10:22 UTC for the next shift. maya handing off. key action items: 1) monitor until burst token expires, 2) schedule post-incident capacity review with NimblePay, 3) follow up on kvcache tuning.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2145 auto-escalated to SRE-Platform after 2 acknowledged escalations.
ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: capture heap/profile and kvcache metrics window `redwood-metrics export --tenant NimblePay --window 00:15:00 --out /tmp/nimble-evictions.json`
jon: ran metrics export and uploaded to /artifacts/INC-2145/nimble-evictions.json.
maya: thanks — assigning postmortem owner: jon. Severity P1 -> postmortem required. I'll notify the incident review channel.
sandeep: tentative root cause: traffic churn from NimblePay batcher + conservative kvcache retention + reserved-pool sizing. action: propose increasing default burst reserve for high-throughput tenants and add dynamic per-tenant kvcache hysteresis.
tara: copied. support + account updated. please ping if any regression.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2145 status: mitigated -> monitoring. will auto-close when stable for 30m or manual close by oncall.
